items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: Professor Harley had taught music in eight schools, so we would see him about fifteen minutes every month, or maybe every other month.

ctx.x: Now, Jackson State College was located on Lynch Street, the same street that my first school was located on -- and it was called Jim Hill. We went from the First Grade through the Ninth Grade at Jim Hill. And some time later, I found out that Jim Hill had been the Secretary of the State of Mississippi during the Reconstruction period. And also, I found out after I got to California that John R. Lynch was the man that Lynch Street was named after, and he was also a Congressman, a Black Congressman during the…

And I had some great teachers, very wonderful people. And later on, after I finished the Ninth Grade, I went to Lanier High School. And they were just beginning to get a school band together. Before then, Professor Harley had taught music in eight schools, so we would see him about fifteen minutes every month, or maybe every other month. So we decided to extend the music program. And Professor Mosely came up from Louisiana, Baton Rouge, Louisiana. He had been teaching at Southern, and he began teaching there.…
